standard.title: Managing changes and transitions
standard.description: refine, evaluate and adapt strategies for managing changes and transitions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can analyse factors that shape identities and evaluate how individuals influence others' identities (AC9HP10P01). They have previously investigated resources and strategies to manage changes including puberty (AC9HP6P02) and analysed the impact of changes and transitions (AC9HP8P02). At Y9-10 the focus shifts to refining, evaluating and adapting — not introducing strategies for the first time.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students refine, evaluate and adapt strategies for managing changes and transitions, including asserting their stance respectfully and responding to changing social and behavioural expectations.

nodes.label: Evaluating existing strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the effectiveness of strategies they have previously used or learned for managing changes and transitions
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one strategy for managing a change or transition and evaluate its effectiveness in a specific situation — what worked, what didn't, and why
nodes.typical_width: Assess behavioural expectations across different relationships and social situations; evaluate how these expectations influence decisions and actions when managing transitions; identify which strategies are most effective for different types of change
wider: Analyse how changing roles and responsibilities for First Nations Australians as social standing changes within communities creates distinct transition challenges — evaluate what strategies are culturally appropriate versus imposed from outside
Investigate the impact of border crossing on identity and transition for First Nations Australians, evaluating the specific strategies needed when navigating between cultural contexts

Evaluate strategies for managing digital transitions (e.g. changing social media presence, online identity shifts) as a distinct category of contemporary transition that existing frameworks may not fully address
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot evaluate the effectiveness of strategies cannot meaningfully refine or adapt them in Node 2 — refinement requires a prior evaluative judgement about what needs to change and why.

response_modes.reason: Students often describe strategies without evaluating them — listing what they would do without assessing whether it works or why. Scaffolding the evaluative move (what was the strategy, in what context, what was the outcome, what does this reveal about when it works) is the key investment here. The First Nations transition contexts require particular care — evaluation must include cultural appropriateness as a criterion, not just effectiveness by generic measures.

success_criteria: Names a specific strategy for managing a change or transition
Evaluates its effectiveness with reference to a specific situation or context
Identifies at least one condition under which the strategy works well and one where it is less effective

nodes.label: Refining and adapting strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can refine and adapt strategies for managing changes and transitions, including asserting their position respectfully in challenging situations
nodes.minimum_width: Rehearse one refined strategy for managing a challenging transition situation; explain what was adapted from a prior approach and why
nodes.typical_width: Practise skills for dealing with challenging or unsafe situations (refusal skills, communicating choices, expressing opinions, contingency plans); rehearse asserting a stance on a dilemma by expressing thoughts and beliefs while acknowledging others' feelings; evaluate which adapted strategies are most effective
wider: Design and rehearse a strategy for asserting a position in a culturally complex transition — e.g. navigating between community and family expectations and individual identity needs

Practise refusal skills and contingency planning for situations involving peer pressure around risk-taking (substance use, unsafe situations), evaluating which communication approaches are most effective in which social contexts
Evaluate how the same adaptive strategy performs differently in face-to-face versus online transition contexts and propose modifications for each

response_modes.reason: Refining and adapting strategies is a capability that builds through practising a range of situations. A single rehearsed scenario is insufficient — students need to build a repertoire of adapted responses across different transition types (social, cultural, online, risk-related) so that the adaptation skill itself becomes flexible. The elaborations explicitly require rehearsal across multiple scenario types.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Culturally complex transitions, peer pressure scenarios, and online versus face-to-face contexts each require genuinely different adaptive strategies — not the same strategy applied in a new setting. Students who work across these wider contexts build adaptive capability that transfers to novel transition situations rather than competence with a single scenario type.
success_criteria: Demonstrates a refined or adapted strategy for a specific transition situation
Explains what was changed from a prior approach and the reasoning for the change
Rehearsed strategy includes acknowledgement of others' perspectives or feelings, not only self-assertion
